import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Create a more descriptive 'survival_status' column for plotting
df['survival_status'] = df['survived'].map({0: 'Did not survive', 1: 'Survived'})

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# --- Visualization ---
# Create a FacetGrid to show relationships between survival, class, sex, and age
g = sns.FacetGrid(df, col="pclass", row="sex", hue="survival_status",
                  height=4, aspect=1.2, margin_titles=True,
                  palette={'Survived': 'seagreen', 'Did not survive': 'indianred'},
                  hue_order=['Survived', 'Did not survive'])

# Map a kernel density plot and a rug plot onto the grid
g.map(sns.kdeplot, "age", fill=True, alpha=.7, lw=2)
g.map(sns.rugplot, "age", height=-.05, clip_on=False)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Add a clear, descriptive title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    'Age Distribution of Titanic Passengers by Survival Status, Sex, and Class',
    fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.03
)

# Set axis labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Age", "Density")

# Adjust titles for each subplot
g.set_titles(row_template="{row_name}", col_template="Class {col_name}")

# Create a custom legend instead of the default FacetGrid one
# This provides more control over placement and appearance
g.fig.subplots_adjust(right=0.85) # Make space for the legend
patch_survived = mpatches.Patch(color='seagreen', label='Survived')
patch_not_survived = mpatches.Patch(color='indianred', label='Did not survive')
g.fig.legend(
    handles=[patch_survived, patch_not_survived],
    title='Survival Status',
    loc='center right',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1, 0.5),
    fontsize='medium',
    title_fontsize='large'
)

# Remove the default FacetGrid legend
g.legend.remove()

# --- Save the Figure ---
# Save the final plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
